comparison: Perfect agreement on CUMS model establishment (C21-C29). Both OpenEval and peer reviewers affirm the behavioral phenotype through multiple validated tests and biochemical markers, with no concerns raised about model validity.

Both address therapeutic implications (C82, C103-C104). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN noting lack of therapeutic validation studies, while peer reviewers implicitly accept these speculative statements without challenge, describing them as 'valuable findings' and 'a new approach to treating osteoporosis.'

Strong agreement on osteoclast-mediated bone loss. OpenEval (C38-C45, C99-C100) and peer reviewers (C2, C30-C31, C38-C45, C99-C100) both affirm increased osteoclast activity as primary mechanism. Peer review additionally groups structural bone deficits (C30-C31) with osteoclast findings, while OpenEval separates these into R2.

Both address structural bone deficits (C30-C31). OpenEval focuses specifically on micro-CT and histological evidence of bone loss. Peer review groups these claims with broader osteoclast findings (C2, C38-C45, C99-C100), affirming the overall bone phenotype.

Agreement on osteoblast findings (C32-C37, C94). Both support the compensatory osteogenic response despite bone loss. OpenEval explicitly discusses incomplete osteoblast maturation; peer reviewers accept findings without challenging the compensatory interpretation. Peer review also includes literature comparison claims (C95-C98) that OpenEval addresses separately in R13.

Both address literature comparison and age-dependent mechanisms (C95-C98). OpenEval notes the proposed compensatory mechanism is reasonable but speculative. Peer reviewers accept these contextual claims as part of the osteoblast characterization without raising concerns.

Agreement on miR-335-3p downregulation in bone (C46-C49). Both affirm sequencing and qRT-PCR validation. OpenEval notes magnitude differences between methods as common; peer reviewers explicitly confirm the finding without concerns. Peer review also includes brain and serum expression (C3, C51-C53) that OpenEval addresses separately in R6.

Both address miR-335-3p expression across tissues (C51-C55, C87-C89). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting correlation but lacking direct evidence of NAC-to-bone transport. Peer reviewers affirm the finding that miR-335-3p is 'simultaneously reduced in murine NAC, serum, and bone' without expressing uncertainty about the transport mechanism.

Partial overlap on NAC-bone connection. OpenEval (C51-C55, C87-C89) expresses uncertainty about direct transport evidence. Peer review (C9-C10, C54-C55, C78-C81, C87-C89, C93, C101-C102) accepts the overall NAC-to-bone mechanism as part of the integrated conclusion without raising transport concerns.

Agreement on miR-335-3p functional role in osteoclasts (C56-C61). Both affirm bidirectional effects of mimic/inhibitor on osteoclast activity through multiple assays. OpenEval emphasizes strong causal evidence; peer reviewers explicitly confirm the functional demonstration. Peer review also includes in vivo effects (C4-C5, C62-C64) that OpenEval addresses separately in R8.

Both address in vivo miR-335-3p effects on bone (C62-C64). OpenEval notes asymmetric effects consistent with necessity but not sufficiency. Peer reviewers affirm the functional role without specifically discussing the asymmetry, grouping these claims with broader in vitro functional data.

Agreement on miR-335-3p targeting of Fos (C65-C66, C69-C71). Both affirm luciferase assays and direct targeting. OpenEval notes incomplete rescue suggests additional complexity; peer reviewers accept the targeting relationship without expressing concerns about complexity.

Agreement on Fos expression changes (C6, C72-C74). Both affirm mRNA-protein discordance as consistent with miRNA regulation. OpenEval emphasizes this strengthens mechanistic interpretation; peer reviewers accept the finding as part of the validated miR-335-3p/Fos pathway.

Agreement on Fos rescue experiments (C7-C8, C75-C77). Both affirm FOS inhibitor T-5224 reverses miR-335-3p inhibitor effects, supporting the miR-335-3p→Fos→osteoclast pathway. OpenEval emphasizes strong pathway evidence; peer reviewers explicitly confirm the demonstrated mechanism.

Agreement on integrated mechanistic conclusion (C2, C9, C78-C81, C93, C101-C102). Both affirm the overall NAC→miR-335-3p→Fos→osteoclast pathway. OpenEval notes direct brain-to-bone transport evidence remains incomplete; peer reviewers accept the mechanism without expressing this caveat, describing 'solid evidence' for the pathway.

Both address novelty claims (C10). OpenEval supports the finding but notes prior work on brain-derived miRNAs affecting bone, suggesting the specific miR-335-3p→Fos pathway in stress-induced osteoporosis is novel. Peer reviewers affirm novelty without qualification, noting the study 'may suggest a new approach.'

OpenEval evaluates background literature claims (C1, C11-C14, C83) as accurately summarizing established knowledge with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; peer reviewers do not separately assess background claims.

OpenEval evaluates literature review claims (C15-C20, C84-C86, C90-C92) establishing rationale for investigating miRNAs as mediators. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; peer reviewers do not separately assess these contextual claims.

OpenEval evaluates claim C50 about prior miR-133a-3p work and apparent discrepancy with current findings. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; peer reviewers do not address this specific literature comparison.

OpenEval evaluates claims C67-C68 citing prior literature on FOS as key osteoclast regulator. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; peer reviewers do not separately assess these background citations.
